name: OdosLimitOrderRouter ERC-6492 signature check makes arbitrary calls
summary: OdosLimitOrderRouter exposed isValidSigImpl() publicly with a caller-chosen allowSideEffects flag; for an ERC-6492 wrapped signature from a signer without code it calls the embedded factory address with the embedded calldata before any signature check. The attacker passed token contracts as the factory and transfer(attacker, balance) as calldata, so the router sent out its own token balances; the same call drained the router's deployments on nine other chains.
notes: Campaign: every transaction on the ten OdosLimitOrderRouter deployments of deployer 0x8eaeeab2 (same bytecode up to immutables) that reached a successful isValidSigImpl or isValidSigWithSideEffects call on the router, found from router outflows not made by its own fill functions and from direct calls, and that took router assets (Sonic 69, Base 33, Arbitrum 25, Optimism 22, Linea 22, Avalanche 17, Polygon 16, BSC 14, Mantle 13, Ethereum 8; 37 further successful calls took nothing). The anchor's sender 0x4015d786 hit Ethereum, Optimism, Arbitrum and Sonic within 20 minutes; the rest are copycats through 2026-08. Sonic has no traces, so its transactions are direct calls plus two routed ones whose router transfers went to the sender. No router outflow before the anchor went through these functions.

Loss is the routers' gross outflow in those transactions (loss.mjs, the ten routers as victims). 38 unpriced tokens (memecoins and wrapped receipts) are listed at 0 because their sales were not traced. The anchor attacker's later swaps of its haul are disposal, not exploits.
